s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of shortness of breath and cardiac dysfunction following chemotherapy and immunotherapy
salient_findings: Elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT, NT-ProBNP)
Poor diastolic function on cardiac color ultrasound
key_facts: Hospitalized due to repeated cough for 2 months
No history of autoimmune diseases, diabetes, hypertension, coronary disease, arrhythmia, chronic heart failure or smoking
Experienced shortness of breath, loss of appetite and weight loss one week after 5th cycle of chemotherapy and immunotherapy
Normal breathing sounds in both lungs
Heart rate: 115 bpm with normal rhythm
Cardiac color ultrasound showed enlarged aorta, normal left ventricular systolic function, poor diastolic function, and small amount of pericardial effusion
Cardiac MR showed mild decline in cardiac function with myocardial edema

shortlist.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced shortness of breath and cardiac dysfunction after immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Cardiotoxicity from chemotherapy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had elevated cardiac biomarkers and myocardial edema after chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had pericardial effusion and elevated cardiac biomarkers

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had normal coronary arteries and cardiac dysfunction

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had cardiac dysfunction and normal coronary arteries

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of shortness of breath, loss of appetite, and weight loss occurred one week after the 5th cycle of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and laboratory tests showed significantly elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT) with myocardial edema on cardiac MR, which is consistent with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis.

rejected.label: Cardiotoxicity from chemotherapy
rejected.why: While chemotherapy can cause cardiotoxicity, the temporal relationship with immunotherapy and the specific pattern of cardiac biomarker elevation and imaging findings point more towards an immune-related mechanism.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: The presence of myocardial edema and elevated cardiac biomarkers suggests myocardial involvement beyond just pericarditis.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no clear stressor identified, and the pattern of cardiac biomarker elevation and imaging findings does not typically match stress cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The lack of a clear stressor and the specific pattern of cardiac biomarker elevation and imaging findings, including myocardial edema, do not support Takotsubo cardiomyopathy as the primary diagnosis.
